Count the corners on a plane window.
Window seat or aisle?
Next time you fly,
count the corners
on your window.
There are none.
In 1954,
the first jet airliner
kept breaking up in midair.
Every flight pumps
the cabin up like
a balloon,
then lets it down.
Around a sharp corner,
all that stretch piles
up in one tiny spot.
Flight after flight,
a crack grew from one
square corner,
until the cabin burst.
Round the corners,
and the stress flows
smoothly around the hole.
